title: A bite on a surface
hook: A meal may be attached instead of swimming away.

doesNotKnow: Some parrotfish use beak-like teeth against a hard surface. What action does this help them perform?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: Some parrotfish use beak-like teeth against a hard surface. What action does this help them perform?

claims.text: Some parrotfish use beak-like teeth against a hard surface. What action does this help them perform? The second panel shows beak-like teeth contacting and scraping a surface. Some parrotfish use fused teeth to scrape or bite food and associated material from hard substrates. Species and diets vary, and the diagram is not a full account of reef feeding.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: NOAA Fisheries, fish anatomy and behavior, https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
An animal has fused teeth suited to removing attached material from a rock. Which action fits that shape? A beak-like surface can help scrape material from a substrate.
